fetch_recipe: GET the recorded url exactly (raw Internet Archive id_ form) with no Accept-Encoding request header and no automatic decoding (for example curl -s -o FILE URL, without --compressed), then hash the bytes as received. A client that sends Accept-Encoding can receive an on-the-fly gzip body with different bytes, and a decoding client unpacks bodies that the archive stores compressed.
stability_check: Raw Internet Archive id_ replay of a fixed capture, fetched with plain curl (no Accept-Encoding, no decoding). First downloaded on 2026-09-28T17:22:22Z; downloaded again at 2026-09-28T18:25:15Z, 2026-09-28T19:04:25Z, the last at least 30 minutes after the first, each with the same byte count and SHA-256 (2781 bytes). The capture's CDX digest does not equal the base32 SHA-1 of the served body, because the capture was archived from a chunked response and the digest covers the stored payload.
provenance_note: Raw Internet Archive capture (id_ form) of the Freedom Front's or Freedom Front Plus's original page, captured at 1998-06-13T21:36:41Z (before the 7 September 2026 cutoff); that form replays the archived bytes unchanged and is used in place of any live copy (the old www.vryheidsfront.co.za pages are no longer served, and the current www.vfplus.org.za pages carry rotating embedded blocks). The response identity recorded here was confirmed by downloads at least 30 minutes apart (see stability_check). This checked-in file is a derived factual extract, not a copy of the original response. Original response bodies and page renders are not checked into this repository. Its own checksum is recorded separately in the packet.

scope_note: Raw Internet Archive capture made 13 June 1998; archived Last-Modified Sat, 13 Jun 1998 21:29:47 GMT. Afrikaans, Windows-1252. The release reacts to another party leader's resignation; that office is not researched here. Served without content encoding. The capture was archived from a chunked response, so its CDX digest does not equal the base32 SHA-1 of the de-chunked body served; the byte count and SHA-256 were stable across downloads.
